additions.site_name: NDC Paris 1 Data Center, Vélizy-Villacoublay (8-10 avenue Morane Saulnier)
additions.name: NDC Paris 1 — 7 MW IT data centre (permit PC 078 640 24 V1008)

status.summary: Altarea's release of 21 October 2026 reports that the group launched works this summer on its 7 MW IT data centre at Vélizy-Villacoublay (headlined as the project's first stone), with delivery to its user expected within 18 months. Its 29 July 2026 half-year report already stated that the group holds a final building permit for the 7 MW IT Vélizy data centre and that works were launched at the end of the half-year. Construction is therefore under way as of the 21 October report; no work stage, completion or operation is asserted, and the delivery horizon is a forecast.

locator.precision: Centroid of the 1.19 ha land of building permit PC 078 640 24 V1008 (current parcels AE 447, AE 532 and AE 533, about 177 by 138 m) at 8-10 avenue Morane Saulnier. The permit covers the data centre together with a student residence and shops, so the point locates the permit plot that contains the data centre, not the data-centre building itself.
locator.identity_review: The SDES register lists permit PC 078 640 24 V1008 to ALTA NDC VELIZY (NAF 63.11Z, data processing and hosting) at 8-10 avenue Morane Saulnier on parcels AE 444 and AE 447 (11,892 m2), creating 10,160 m2 of housing and 5,579 m2 of non-residential floor; this matches Altarea's NDC Paris 1 data centre with its neighbouring Cogedim student residence and its 'Alta NDC' project-company naming (SNC ALTA NDC NOYAL at Noyal). AE 444 is absent from the current cadastre; AE 532 (5,663 m2) and AE 533 (5,761 m2) sum to 11,424 m2, equal within 1 m2 to the permit land less AE 447 (469 m2), and with AE 447 form one contiguous polygon fronting avenue Morane Saulnier, so they are taken as the successors of AE 444: of all combinations of up to five other parcels in the queried box whose areas with AE 447 total the permit land within 10 m2, only AE 532 + AE 533 is contiguous with AE 447. The avenue's street-level geocoder point is not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is the centroid of a 1.2 ha mixed-use plot whose vertices lie up to 117 m away, the data-centre building's position within it is not published, and the successor parcels of AE 444 are inferred from area and adjacency rather than from a published parcel filiation.

Its 29 July 2026 half-year report describes the same Noyal data centre as one of two Altarea data centres in operation near Rennes, inaugurated in October 2025 and holding all the certifications needed for its operation and marketing. The data centre is therefore operating and fully let as of the 21 October report; the statement says nothing about utilisation of the 3 MW IT.

The Géorisques register point, 105 m outside the parcel, is not used.

additions.name: Project Thunderbird West Campus — proposed data center on the western tract (rezoning A to I-3)

status.summary: On 27 August 2026 the City of Enid received Plainsmen Holdings, LLC's application to rezone the Project Thunderbird West Campus western quarter, the SW/4 of Section 16, T22N, R6W (Indian Meridian), Garfield County, about 159 acres less a 183 by 187 ft excepted tract, from A Agricultural to I-3 Industrial (Heavy) for heavy industrial use 'which may include data center and associated support facilities', with no electric generating facility proposed on the property. It is one of three coordinated Project Thunderbird rezoning applications. The application is not a consent: the Planning Commission's 28 September recommendation is advisory, the City Commission decides on 27 October 2026, and the City states that no data-center site plan, intensive-use application or construction approval has been submitted, so no permit, site work or construction is established.

locator.precision: Centroid of Garfield County parcel 0000-16-22N-06W-3-100-00 (the SW/4 of Section 16, T22N, R6W less the 183 by 187 ft southwest-corner tract; 158.77 geodesic acres, about 0.81 by 0.81 km), from the City of Enid's GC_Parcels service. It locates the West Campus western rezoning tract, not a data-centre building, a site plan or any works, and excludes the I-2 transition tract to the east.
locator.identity_review: The Enid MAPC agenda of 28 September 2026 (items 10-11) names Parcel ID 0000-16-22N-06W-3-100-00 for this exact request, and the parcel's roll legal description repeats the application's description, including the SW-corner exception, which is the separate 1-acre parcel 0000-16-22N-06W-3-625-00. The applicant's area map places the tract between S 16th St and S 30th St north of E Rupe Ave, matching the parcel polygon. The county roll's owner predates the 2 April 2026 deed recording to Two Boots Land and Cattle, LLC, so identity rests on the parcel ID and legal description, not the owner field.
locator.uncertainty_reason: County parcel polygons carry no published positional accuracy; the centroid represents a quarter-section tract about 0.81 km across, and no building position has been proposed.

additions.site_name: OKC2 (6000 N Shartel Ave, Oklahoma City)
additions.name: OKC2 — GPU computing data center with on-site gas-engine power (proposed new facility)

status.summary: On 21 September 2026 the Oklahoma DEQ Air Quality Division confirmed that 6000 N Shartel Ave, LLC had filed, on 4 September 2026, an administratively complete application for a major source construction permit (MAC000520) for OKC2, a facility classified as SIC 7374 / NAICS 518210 (data processing and hosting) in Section 9, T12N, R3W, Oklahoma County. DEQ's July 2026 evaluation of the facility's earlier minor-source application states that OKC2 'will be a newly constructed facility' whose island-mode natural-gas engines and battery banks are to power GPU-based computing. The application covers engine emissions only; it is not consent for the data-centre development, and no construction, completion or operation is established.

locator.precision: Facility coordinate printed in the Oklahoma DEQ evaluation memorandum for permit 2026-0216-C (35.53351 N, 97.52242 W, five decimal places, no datum stated), inside the NE/4 NW/4 of Section 9, T12N, R3W (Indian Meridian) named by DEQ. It locates the permitted OKC2 facility as reported to the regulator, not a surveyed building footprint or the leased site's boundary.
locator.identity_review: The DEQ memorandum of 23 July 2026 (permit 2026-0216-C) and DEQ's letter of 21 September 2026 (MAC000520) name the same permittee, 6000 N Shartel Ave, LLC, the same facility, OKC2 (Facility ID 25431, SIC 7374 / NAICS 518210), and the same Section 9, T12N, R3W. The BLM CadNSDI PLSS service places the coordinate in Section 09, T12N, R3W, aliquot NE/4 NW/4, in the north part of the section, and the memorandum's directions put the site on the east side of N Shartel Ave north of I-44, consistent with the permittee's name. No parcel polygon could be used: the City of Oklahoma City GIS returned a bot challenge and the county assessor's robots.txt returned HTTP 403.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The memorandum gives no datum, collection method or accuracy for the applicant-reported facility coordinate, and the size of the leased site is not published.

status.summary: In its release of 5 October 2026 IIJ states that the large-capacity lithium-ion batteries installed at its IIJ Matsue Data Center Park are operated as backup power for the data-centre facilities, and commits about 1,000 kWh of that stored power to Matsue City's evacuation shelters under a disaster power-supply agreement concluded that day. This is the operator's present-tense description of the existing campus in service on 5 October 2026. It establishes no new building, phase, capacity, utilisation or construction; the planned disaster drills are future work.
